'''Jan Peter Toennies''' (born 3 May 1930) is a German-American scientist, known for his contributions to molecular physics, surface scattering, and the development of helium nanodroplet spectroscopy.

==Early life and education==
Toennies was born in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]] on 3 May 1930 to German immigrant parents.<ref name=":0" />  He is the grandson of sociologist [[Ferdinand Tönnies]]. He graduated from [[Lower Merion High School]], outside of Philadelphia, in 1948. He went on to [[Amherst College]], where he received a B.A. in 1952, and to [[Brown University]], where he received a Ph.D. in chemistry in 1957. During graduate school he was a [[Fulbright|Fulbright student]] in [[Göttingen]] 1953–1954.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
After graduation in 1957 he moved to the Physics Department of the [[University of Bonn]] where he was a postdoctoral researcher with [[Wolfgang Paul]]. In 1965 he obtained the [[Habilitation]] in experimental physics, becoming an assistant professor,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Toennies |first=J. Peter |date=2011-06-30 |title=Autobiography of Jan Peter Toennies |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/jp201144y |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A |volume=115 |issue=25 |pages=6742–6745 |doi=10.1021/jp201144y |issn=1089-5639}}</ref> as well as a guest professor in the Department of Physical Chemistry at the Gothenburg University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A garden of physics – 70 alumni from different fields of science congratulate |url=https://www.ds.mpg.de/2740246/150513_toennies_jan |access-date=2026-02-08 |website=www.ds.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref> In 1969 he became director at the [[Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization|Max Planck Institute for Fluid Dynamics]]. From 1971 he was a professor in Göttingen and honorary professor at the University of Bonn. He retired officially in 1998, but was acting director until 2004.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
{{primary sources|section|date=February 2026}}
Toennies measured total and inelastic [[Cross section (physics)|collision cross sections]] for transitions between rotational states of various gases with quantum-state resolution.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Toennies |first=J. P. |date=1965-06-01 |title=Molekularstrahlmessungen von Stoßquerschnitten für Übergänge zwischen definierten Rotationszuständen zwei-atomiger Moleküle |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01383864 |journal=Zeitschrift für Physik |language=de |volume=182 |issue=3 |pages=257–277 |doi=10.1007/BF01383864 |issn=0044-3328|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He investigated vibrational excitation of H<sub>2</sub> in central collisions with Lithium ions using the [[Time-of-flight mass spectrometry|time-of-flight method]], as well as dissociation in single collision events.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schöttler |first=J. |last2=Toennies |first2=J. P. |year=1968 |title=Molekularstrahlmessungen zur Untersuchung der Schwingungsanregung von H 2 beim Stoß mit Li + ‐Ionen |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/bbpc.19680720816 |journal=Berichte der Bunsengesellschaft für physikalische Chemie |language=en |volume=72 |issue=8 |pages=979–983 |doi=10.1002/bbpc.19680720816 |issn=0005-9021|url-access=subscription }}</ref> In Göttingen, his group solved the [[Boltzmann equation]] while accounting for quantum effects and realistic interaction potentials in helium free-jet expansion, and proposed an improved model for [[van der Waals potential]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Tang |first=K. T. |last2=Toennies |first2=J. Peter |date=1984-04-15 |title=An improved simple model for the van der Waals potential based on universal damping functions for the dispersion coefficients |url=https://pubs.aip.org/jcp/article/80/8/3726/90054/An-improved-simple-model-for-the-van-der-Waals |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |language=en |volume=80 |issue=8 |pages=3726–3741 |doi=10.1063/1.447150 |issn=0021-9606|url-access=subscription }}</ref> referred to as Tang-Toennies model.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Nitzke |first=Isabel |last2=Pohl |first2=Sven |last3=Thol |first3=Monika |last4=Span |first4=Roland |last5=Vrabec |first5=Jadran |date=2022-06-03 |title=How well does the Tang-Toennies potential represent the thermodynamic properties of argon? |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00268976.2022.2078240 |journal=Molecular Physics |language=en |volume=120 |issue=11 |doi=10.1080/00268976.2022.2078240 |issn=0026-8976|url-access=subscription }}</ref> High-resolution measurements of surface phonon dispersion for Ag,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Doak |first=R. B. |last2=Harten |first2=U. |last3=Toennies |first3=J. Peter |date=1983-08-15 |title=Anomalous Surface Phonon Dispersion Relations for Ag(111) Measured by Inelastic Scattering of He Atoms |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.578 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=51 |issue=7 |pages=578–581 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.51.578 |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref> LiF, NaF, KCl,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Brusdeylins |first=G. |last2=Doak |first2=R. Bruce |last3=Toennies |first3=J. Peter |date=1983-03-15 |title=High-resolution helium time-of-flight studies of Rayleigh surface-phonon dispersion curves of LiF, NaF, and KCl |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.27.3662 |journal=Physical Review B |language=en |volume=27 |issue=6 |pages=3662–3685 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.27.3662 |issn=0163-1829|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and Pt-crystals<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Harten |first=U. |last2=Toennies |first2=J. Peter |last3=Wöll |first3=Christof |last4=Zhang |first4=G. |date=1985-11-18 |title=Observation of a Kohn Anomaly in the Surface-Phonon Dispersion Curves of Pt(111) |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2308 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=55 |issue=21 |pages=2308–2311 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.55.2308 |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref> were carried out using inelastic scattering of helium atoms. The group achieved non-destructive detection of fragile He, H<sub>2</sub> and D<sub>2</sub> clusters by utilizing diffraction from nanoscopic transmission gratings.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Schöllkopf |first=Wieland |last2=Toennies |first2=J. Peter |date=1994-11-25 |title=Nondestructive Mass Selection of Small van der Waals Clusters |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.266.5189.1345 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=266 |issue=5189 |pages=1345–1348 |doi=10.1126/science.266.5189.1345 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref> A spectroscopic study of SF<sub>6</sub> doped in helium [[Nano-droplets|nanodroplets]] revealed sharp spectral features of the embedded molecule. This indicated that the molecule was extremely cold and that it resides in its ground state at a temperature of 0.37 K, practically unaffected by the helium environment and could rotate freely as if in a vacuum.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hartmann |first=M. |last2=Miller |first2=R. E. |last3=Toennies |first3=J. P. |last4=Vilesov |first4=A. |date=1995-08-21 |title=Rotationally Resolved Spectroscopy of S F 6 in Liquid Helium Clusters: A Molecular Probe of Cluster Temperature |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1566 |journal=Physical Review Letters |language=en |volume=75 |issue=8 |pages=1566–1569 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.75.1566 |issn=0031-9007|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Subsequent spectroscopic experiments demonstrated that the free rotations were related to the microscopic [[superfluidity]] of helium droplets,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grebenev |first=Slava |last2=Toennies |first2=J. Peter |last3=Vilesov |first3=Andrei F. |date=1998-03-27 |title=Superfluidity Within a Small Helium-4 Cluster: The Microscopic Andronikashvili Experiment |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.279.5359.2083 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=279 |issue=5359 |pages=2083–2086 |doi=10.1126/science.279.5359.2083 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and, for the first time, of a small numbers of hydrogen molecules.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grebenev |first=Slava |last2=Sartakov |first2=Boris |last3=Toennies |first3=J. Peter |last4=Vilesov |first4=Andrei F. |year=2000 |title=Evidence for Superfluidity in Para-Hydrogen Clusters Inside Helium-4 Droplets at 0.15 Kelvin |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.289.5484.1532 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=289 |issue=5484 |pages=1532–1535 |doi=10.1126/science.289.5484.1532 |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
